correctness.rationale: For all d>=1, 0<α<β and 0<r<infinity, full-cross-ratio simplex distance equals the range of m=d+1 independent log-gamma ratios. The density and characteristic function follow from beta-prime and Euler Gamma identities. A convergent independent Bernoulli–Laplace series factors the α characteristic function through the β law; Prékopa log-concavity bounds every convex symmetric range event. Real analyticity and eventual vanishing along every nonconstant translation give strictness; the noise vector is nonconstant with positive probability. The boundary limits and α=1 benchmark follow independently. check.py and check.log corroborate the derivation, but finite checks do not replace proof.

value.rationale: Hilbert distance diverges near simplex facets, while Dirichlet concentration controls mass toward the barycenter in ordinary barycentric coordinates. The theorem gives a simultaneous strict stochastic law at every finite positive radius, in every simplex dimension and independent of Euclidean shape, not only isolated moments. Its explicit all-real-parameter additive-noise coupling supplies a reusable mechanism for symmetric convex log-ratio events and sharp 0/infinity concentration boundary behavior.
